data.name: Import_Intro
data.value: Paste a crosshair code from CS2 (CSGO-xxxxx-xxxxx-…), Valorant (0;P;c;5;…) or a CrossGOverlay image crosshair code (CGO-IMG;…). The format is detected automatically.

data.name: Export_Cs2Console
data.value: Console commands (paste into the console or autoexec.cfg)

data.name: Export_ImageNotSupported
data.value: Games do not accept image crosshairs, so there is no code for this format.

data.name: Export_ValorantNote
data.value: Paste into Valorant: Settings → Crosshair → Import Profile Code. Every setting converts exactly.

data.name: Export_ValorantLossy
data.value: Paste into Valorant: Settings → Crosshair → Import Profile Code. This preset uses features Valorant cannot describe (ring, square, rotation, diagonal lines or rounded caps), so the code differs slightly.

data.name: Export_Cs2Note
data.value: Paste into CS2: Settings → Game → Crosshair → Share or Import. Sizes are approximate because CS2 scales the crosshair with resolution and FOV.

data.name: Export_Cs2Lossy
data.value: Paste into CS2: Settings → Game → Crosshair → Share or Import. CS2 has a single line layer and no ring or rotation, so the code keeps only the closest match.

data.name: Export_AppNote
data.value: Keeps everything, including what neither game supports. Send it to another CrossGOverlay user and “Import code” gives them this exact preset.

data.name: Export_AppNoteImage
data.value: The code carries the image itself. The recipient clicks “Import code” and pastes it to get this crosshair.

data.name: Import_Accuracy
data.value: Structure (shape, colour, centre dot, outline) converts exactly. Sizes are approximate because the games use different units — adjust the Scale slider after importing if needed.
